title: Fever and Rash
hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with fever, sore throat, and a diffuse erythematous sandpaper-like rash that blanches with pressure. Exam reveals strawberry tongue (initially white-coated then red), pharyngeal erythema with exudates, and Pastia lines (linear petechiae in skin folds). Caused by Group A Streptococcus pyogenes producing erythrogenic exotoxin. Diagnosis: rapid strep test or throat culture. Treatment: penicillin VK PO x 10 days or amoxicillin (first-line). If penicillin-allergic: cephalexin or clindamycin. Complete full course to prevent acute rheumatic fever (not PSGN — which occurs after skin infection). Children can return to school 24h after starting antibiotics.
